rationale: C10 is the clearest drafting template. The child closely reproduces its opening sequence and distinctive evaluative language: review of a transmitted report, praise of plans as a constructive step toward strengthening an identified governmental process, endorsement of intensified departmental and agency efforts, and approval of giving greater emphasis to the relevant coordinating work. C05 is substantively important because it created Bragdon's position and specified the same public-works coordination mission, but its language and structure are less directly replicated. C13 shares the Federal-State-local public-works planning framework but not comparably distinctive drafting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: There has now been opportunity for me to review the report of your activities ... transmitted in your [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE].
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I have reviewed your analysis of the Hoover Commission's Report on Budget and Accounting, transmitted with your [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE].
shared_material.explanation: Nearly identical opening machinery: presidential review of a subordinate's report or analysis transmitted by an earlier communication.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your plans and proposals represent a constructive forward step toward the achievement of our objective of strengthening and improving the coordination of long-range planning of public works
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Your plans for carrying out the Commission's recommendations represent a constructive approach toward realizing the Commission's objective of strengthening the budget and accounting processes of the Federal Government.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive shared sentence frame praising plans as a constructive means toward an objective of strengthening a governmental process.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I also concur with your findings as to the desirability and necessity of having the Executive departments and agencies intensify their planning efforts
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I consider it desirable and necessary that the executive departments and agencies intensify their efforts
shared_material.explanation: Close lexical correspondence involving desirability and necessity, Executive departments and agencies, and intensified efforts.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Your plan to give greater emphasis at this time to the coordination of public works planning by the Federal agencies seems to me correct.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I approve of your plans to have the Bureau of the Budget give greater emphasis in its work to the evaluation and advancement of administration in the executive agencies
shared_material.explanation: Both endorse a subordinate's plan to give greater emphasis to an administrative coordination or improvement function involving executive agencies.
